description: Schneier discusses the security risks of the internet of things, where connected devices control physical systems. He explains why insecurity persists and argues for government regulation and better design. Thought-provoking reading on technology policy.

title: The Shellcoder's Handbook
author: Chris Anley
description: A technical guide to finding and exploiting security vulnerabilities in software, including stack and heap overflows, format string bugs and shellcode on several platforms. Aimed at advanced security researchers.

title: Linux Basics for Hackers
author: OccupyTheWeb
description: An introduction to Linux for aspiring security professionals, covering the command line, file system, permissions, processes, networking, scripting and anonymity tools on Kali Linux. Suitable for beginners.

title: Threat Modeling
author: Adam Shostack
description: Adam Shostack explains how to identify and address security threats while designing software. He covers frameworks such as STRIDE, diagrams, attack trees and integrating threat modelling into development. Practical for developers and security teams.

title: We Are Anonymous
author: Parmy Olson
description: Parmy Olson reports on the hacktivist collective Anonymous and its offshoot LulzSec, based on interviews with members. She describes their methods, motivations and eventual arrests. An inside look at online activism and hacking.

title: Superintelligence
author: Nick Bostrom
description: Nick Bostrom examines what might happen if machines surpass human intelligence, exploring possible paths to superintelligence, its risks and strategies for keeping it aligned with human interests. A central work in debates on AI safety.

title: Life 3.0
author: Max Tegmark
description: Max Tegmark considers how artificial intelligence could change work, law, warfare and society, and what kind of future humanity should aim for. He discusses both near-term issues and long-term possibilities. An accessible introduction to debates about AI.

title: Human Compatible
author: Stuart Russell
description: Stuart Russell, co-author of a leading AI textbook, argues that AI systems should be designed to be uncertain about human objectives and to defer to people. He explains risks from misaligned AI and proposes a new approach. Important reading on AI safety.

title: The Alignment Problem
author: Brian Christian
description: Brian Christian explores the challenge of making machine learning systems behave as intended. He covers bias, fairness, transparency, reinforcement learning and learning from human preferences through interviews with researchers. Accessible for general readers.

title: Prediction Machines
author: Ajay Agrawal
description: Three economists explain AI as a technology that makes prediction cheap, and show how this changes decision-making, jobs and business strategy. Useful for managers and students of business and economics.

title: AI Superpowers
author: Kai-Fu Lee
publisher: Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Trade & Reference Publishers
description: Kai-Fu Lee compares the development of artificial intelligence in China and the United States and discusses its likely effects on jobs and society. He also reflects on the human qualities that machines cannot replace. A perspective on the global AI landscape.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Guide for Thinking Humans
author: Melanie Mitchell
description: Melanie Mitchell explains how current AI systems work, including deep learning for vision, games and language, and where they still fall short. She separates real progress from hype. Clear reading for students and general audiences.

title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
author: Trevor Hastie
description: A comprehensive textbook on statistical methods for machine learning, covering linear models, classification, kernel methods, model assessment, trees, boosting, neural networks, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Aimed at graduate students with mathematical background.

title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
author: Gareth James
description: An accessible introduction to statistical learning methods such as regression, classification, resampling, regularisation, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Each chapter includes labs in R or Python. Suited to undergraduates and practitioners.

title: Machine Learning
author: Tom M. Mitchell
description: Tom Mitchell's classic textbook introducing the main approaches to machine learning, including concept learning, decision trees, neural networks, Bayesian learning, instance-based learning and reinforcement learning. Clear and concise for students.

title: Machine Learning: A Probabilistic Perspective
author: Kevin P. Murphy
description: A comprehensive textbook presenting machine learning through probabilistic models, covering Bayesian methods, graphical models, Gaussian processes, mixture models and deep learning foundations. Intended for advanced students and researchers.

title: Speech and Language Processing
author: Daniel Jurafsky
description: A leading textbook on natural language processing and speech recognition, covering language models, parsing, semantics, machine translation, dialogue and neural methods. Used in university NLP courses.

title: Probabilistic Graphical Models
author: Daphne Koller
description: A detailed textbook on representing and reasoning with uncertainty using Bayesian networks and Markov networks. It covers representation, inference and learning. Aimed at graduate students and researchers.

title: Data Science from Scratch
author: Joel Grus
description: Joel Grus teaches data science fundamentals by implementing tools in plain Python, including statistics, gradient descent, regression, clustering, neural networks and recommender systems. Good for learners who want to understand methods from the ground up.

title: Python Data Science Handbook
author: Jake VanderPlas
description: A practical reference to the core Python data science stack: IPython, NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and scikit-learn. It shows how to clean, analyse and visualise data and build machine learning models. Suitable for students and analysts.

title: Deep Learning for Coders with fastai and PyTorch
author: Jeremy Howard
description: A hands-on introduction to deep learning for programmers, using the fastai library and PyTorch to build models for images, text, tabular data and recommendations. It explains the theory progressively through code. Suitable for developers without advanced mathematics.

title: Natural Language Processing with Python
author: Steven Bird
description: An introduction to natural language processing using Python and the Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK). It covers accessing text corpora, tokenisation, tagging, classification, parsing and semantics. Suitable for students in linguistics and computing.

title: The Book of Why
author: Judea Pearl
description: Judea Pearl and Dana Mackenzie explain the science of cause and effect, describing causal diagrams and how they help answer questions that data alone cannot. The book discusses implications for statistics and AI. Accessible reading on causal reasoning.
